This page collects the five-part AffineDrift theory series on modeling the golf swing as a control-affine dynamical system. The series is the main entry point for definitions, notation, counterfactual constructions, and the stated limits of the framework.

::: {.callout-note}
## Provenance and status

The control-affine form $\dot{x} = f(x) + g(x)u$ is standard nonlinear-systems material. The site's golf-specific decomposition, zero-torque counterfactual (ZTCF), zero-velocity counterfactual (ZVCF), and drift-control interpretation are original AffineDrift synthesis. These pages should therefore be read as technical working manuscripts rather than as peer-reviewed consensus.
:::

## How to use this series

- Start with Part 1 for the model boundary, state definition, and affine derivation.
- Use Part 2 for the drift/input decomposition and the counterfactual constructions used throughout the site.
- Read Parts 3 and 4 for invariance questions, longer derivations, and supporting examples.
- Use Part 5 for implementation details and Simulink-oriented documentation.
- Keep [Critiques & Responses](../critiques/index.html) nearby when you want the strongest objections, unresolved questions, and scope limits.

## Series contents

### [Theory Part 1 - State definition and affine derivation](../articles/theory-part1.html)

Defines the state, states the modeling assumptions, and derives the control-affine form used across the AffineDrift series.

### [Theory Part 2 - Drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, and ZVCF](../articles/theory-part2.html)

Introduces the separation between state-dependent dynamics and modeled inputs, together with the local counterfactual constructions used to interpret that separation.

### [Theory Part 3 - Drift invariance and taxonomy](../articles/theory-part3.html)

Develops classification language, invariance questions, and scope conditions for the framework.

### [Theory Part 4 - Modal approximation, wrenches, and pendulum examples](../articles/theory-part4.html)

Collects longer derivations and worked examples that support the main framework and show where approximations enter.

### [Theory Part 5 - Simulink model documentation](../articles/theory-part5.html)

Documents implementation choices, simulation structure, and technical notes needed to reproduce the site's Simulink-oriented workflow.

## Evidence and scope

The strongest claims in this series are claims about what follows from a stated model. Interpretive claims about causation, skill, or motor control are weaker whenever they depend on unvalidated parameters, coordinate choices, or assumptions that are not independently supported by data on the page.

For the broader inventory, use the [Article Index](../resources/articles.html). For the two main textbook-scale entry points, use [The Physics of Golf](../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/index.html) and [The Geometry of Motion](../articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/index.html).
